summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing: Clothing Detail Section Update P18 ## Introduction Hello everyone, I am Xueli. In this tutorial video, we will learn how to use the Freeze and Reverse Fire functions in Marvelous Designer. ## Opening the File First, we open the attached file. After opening the file, we can see how to use the Freeze and Reverse Fire versions. ## Understanding the Freeze Function Let's take a look at the function of the Freeze version. After selecting the version, right-click on the selected version and select the Freeze option. When the version is frozen, its shape will continue to remain in 3D space, and it will still be in contact with other versions. You can see that when I turn on the simulation, the semi-transparent version is still hanging on the frozen version. ### Key Points about Freeze - When the version is frozen, it remains in the current state in 3D space. - It does not participate in the simulation but remains in contact with other versions. - To remove the frozen state of a version, select it and right-click to choose the Freeze or Reverse Fire option. The color of the frozen version will return to normal. ## Exploring the Reverse Fire Function Next, let's take a look at how to use the Reverse Fire function. The Reverse Fire function is similar to the Freeze version. After selecting the version, right-click on the menu to find this function. When we apply Reverse Fire to the version, it will show a semi-transparent dark blue. When we turn on the simulation, we will see that these two versions will remain in their current state, but other versions will pass through them. This means that when we apply Reverse Fire to a version, it will not participate in any simulation. ### Activating a Version If you want to activate the version, right-click on it and select Activate. You can see that the version returns to its original state. There are two options in our right-click menu: 1. Reverse Fire Version 2. Reverse Fire Version and Frozen State The difference between them is that if you select the Reverse Fire Version and the Frozen State, the frozen state between the versions will also be reversed. ## Comparison of Freeze and Reverse Fire Let’s take a look at the comparison. First, we created the frozen state between the versions using the line freezing tool. Then we select the pink version and right-click to select the Reverse Fire Version. Here we do not select the Reverse Fire Version. The next version is the same; we use the line freezing tool to create the frozen state between them first. After creating it, we select the Reverse Fire Version and the Frozen State on the right side of the version. After we select the Reverse Fire Version and the Frozen State, we will see that the frozen state between the versions becomes white. When pressing the control key to open the simulation, we will see that if we select the Reverse Fire and the Frozen State, then the frozen state between the versions will no longer work. On the other hand, if the frozen state still works, the versions will freeze each other, but they can still penetrate. ## Practical Application of Reverse Fire and Frozen State Next, let’s practice the function of the Reverse Fire and Frozen State. First, we double-click to enter a new version, then double-click to enter a male virtual model. Next, we double-click to open a T-shirt file in the Gamut folder in the Library window, followed by a pants file. ### Adjusting the Loading Type Note that the loading type here should be set to increase; otherwise, it will cover the previous clothes. We will click No because we don't need to load the size of the virtual model that corresponds to the original clothing. Sometimes, if we want to directly put the clothes into the pants, we may choose to add a layer to the pants. Increase the layer of the pants to be higher than the clothes, so the pants will automatically be worn outside the clothes. ### Managing Stability During Wearing Process However, sometimes it may be unstable during the wearing process. Generally, in such cases, we may first re-enable the pants version. The re-enabled pants version will not affect the top. Next, we will select the version that interacts with the pants in the top. We will reduce its tail-axis shrink in the property editor to make it a tight dress. The shrinkage is divided into front and back. To distinguish the front from the back, we switch to the Edit Text tool. After selecting this version, the arrow direction indicates our front. In Marvelous Designer, the 2D version created typically has its vertical direction as the front and horizontal direction as the back. ### Final Adjustments We need to narrow these versions in the horizontal direction. By reducing the tail-axis shrink to 80, the clothes become a tight dress. Select all the top clothes, right-click, and freeze them to prevent participation in the simulation without changing shape. The pants will still be bumpy. Then, select all the pants in the 2D window, press Shift-Q to display the pants, and right-click to select Activate Pants. Since the pants were reactivated, we can now increase their level and start the simulation with the control button. ## Adding Layers with Down Jackets If we want to add a down jacket on the outside of this dress, how do we manage the layer relationship? After opening the down jacket, we will see the parts of the down jacket and the down jacket itself. If we directly apply a layer to the down jacket, mutual simulation may cause instability. If the down jacket file is complicated, conflicts are likely to occur. ### Processing Layers We can return to when the clothes were just poured in by pressing Ctrl-Z. First, we reverse activate the outer down jacket, ensuring it does not intersect with the inner down jacket during simulation. We need to select all the T-shirt sheets and reduce their tail shrinkage to 80%. Once the entire outfit becomes tighter, we select the top and pants together, then freeze them. Press Shift-Q to display the hidden down jacket. Apply layer 1 to the down jacket to wear it as a whole, adding a little wear and tear outside the clothes and pants. ### Final Adjustments to Shrinkage Once the model is stable, we can freeze the outer layer of the down jacket and hide it. Note that the hidden down jacket will not participate in the simulation; it is merely hidden. We then gradually increase the T-shirt shrinkage from 80 to 100. Since the outer layer of the down jacket is frozen, it will remain limited to the T-shirt inside, allowing us to safely increase the shrinkage. Finally, we activate the outer layer of the down jacket, allowing it and the T-shirt to simulate each other again. This prevents instability after the final adjustments. ## Impact of Frozen and Back-Activated Panels on Simulation Speed Let’s examine how frozen and back-activated panels impact our simulation speed. When our top is a down jacket, the large panels may cause slower operation speeds during simulation. If the down jacket and T-shirt panels are simulated together, dragging the T-shirt panels can slow down the process. However, if we freeze the down jacket panels, they will not be involved in the simulation and will only provide collision, improving simulation speed. If we apply Reverse Fire to the outer layer of the down jacket, the calculations will decrease significantly, leading to a smooth simulation when dragging the T-shirt panels. ## Conclusion In normal use, making effective decisions about these tools can help improve the operation speed of the software. ### Reminder Once you freeze the panels, do not adjust them while in the frozen state. Adjusting panels in this state can lead to unintended transformations in the simulation. Thank you for watching, and see you in the next video. Bye bye! ```
